known_final_diagnosis: The diagnosis of GPA was based on the presence of suggestive clinical signs, notably the notion of hemoptysis, anemia, and suggestive appearance in the scan: multifocal ground glass with respect for the periphery, association of septal lines (crazy paving), and the presence of siderophages in the BAL. The diagnosis was also based on the American College of Rheumatology (ACR)/European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) 2022 classification criteria: the presence of c-ANCA and chest X-ray abnormalities (5 points) (Figure 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old female with 20-year exposure to poultry (canaries and parakeets) and essential oil vapors presented with stage II dyspnea, low-grade hemoptysis for one year, and chronic anemia. Initial empiric treatment with antibiotics (C3G + levofloxacin) and corticosteroids was ineffective. On admission, CT chest revealed diffuse bilateral ground glass opacities with septal and non-septal thickening in a crazy paving pattern, more marked in upper lobes with subpleural sparing, consistent with alveolar hemorrhage. BAL with Perls' staining demonstrated histiocytic macrophagic alveolitis with hemosiderosis (siderophages). Immunological workup revealed c-ANCA positivity (>1/20 U) with negative p-ANCA. Laboratory studies showed normochromic normocytic regenerative anemia, negative 24-hour proteinuria, and normal blood urea. These findings met ACR/EULAR 2022 classification criteria for GPA (c-ANCA and chest X-ray abnormalities = 5 points). After GPA diagnosis confirmation, the patient received high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (1,000 mg/day for 3 consecutive days) followed by oral prednisone with progressive dose reduction to 10 mg/day maintenance. Clinical response was favorable with resolution of asthenia and cough, and improvement in oxygen saturation. Corticosteroids were subsequently eliminated and treatment continued with another immunosuppressive agent.

BAL demonstrates siderophages (hemosiderin-laden macrophages) consistent with alveolar hemorrhage
c-ANCA positive (>1/20 U) with negative p-ANCA, strongly suggesting GPA

Favorable clinical response to high-dose corticosteroid therapy with resolution of asthenia, cough, and improved oxygen saturation

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While exposure history is present, the c-ANCA positivity, hemoptysis, and systemic anemia are not typical of hypersensitivity pneumonitis. The imaging pattern of alveolar hemorrhage with siderophages on BAL is more consistent with vasculitis than hypersensitivity pneumonitis.

Initial antibiotic therapy (C3G + levofloxacin) was ineffective, and BAL findings show alveolitis with hemosiderosis rather than infectious organisms. c-ANCA positivity excludes infection as primary diagnosis.

c-ANCA positivity with negative p-ANCA is characteristic of GPA rather than microscopic polyangiitis (MPA, which is typically p-ANCA/MPO-positive) or eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA).
